subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Porsche's Endurance Dynasty
description: A short lesson to help you apply Porsche's Endurance Dynasty.

hook.text: Porsche has won Le Mans 19 times—more than any other manufacturer in the race's 100-year history.

buildup.text: From the tiny 550 Spyder to the mighty 919 Hybrid, Porsche built its brand around endurance wins.

discovery.text: The 917 in 1970 gave Porsche its first overall Le Mans win—and featured in the iconic Steve McQueen film.

twist.text: Porsche quit Le Mans in 2017 after three straight wins, claiming it had nothing left to prove.

climax.text: It returned in 2023 with a new hybrid hypercar, because Le Mans always pulls the best teams back.

punchline.text: Porsche and Le Mans can't quit each other.

quiz.question: How many times has Porsche won the 24 Hours of Le Mans?

details.summary: Porsche holds the record for the most overall wins at the 24 Hours of Le Mans with 19 victories, dominating endurance racing through decades of engineering continuity and a relentless racing culture.
details.whyItMatters: Porsche's Le Mans success directly feeds into its road car reputation for durability and performance. Endurance racing is the ultimate test of the reliability that Porsche sells to consumers.
takeaways: Porsche has 19 overall victories at Le Mans, more than any manufacturer
The 917, 956, and 919 Hybrid are legendary Le Mans winners
Endurance racing culture permeates Porsche's road car engineering

faq.question: What was Porsche's most iconic Le Mans car?
faq.answer: The 917 from 1970 to 1971 gave Porsche its first overall wins. The flat-12 engine producing over 600 HP and Steve McQueen's Le Mans film made the 917 perhaps the most famous racing Porsche ever.

faq.question: Does Porsche still compete at Le Mans?
faq.answer: Yes. After a brief hiatus, Porsche returned to the top class in 2023 with the 963 LMDh prototype, continuing its commitment to endurance racing alongside programs in Formula E and customer racing.
